abstract.p: We investigate two natural relaxations of quantum cryptographic primitives. The first involves quantum input sampling, where inputs are generated by a quantum algorithm rather than sampled uniformly at random. Applying this to pseudorandom generators (PRGs) and pseudorandom states (PRSs), leads to the notions denoted as PRG qs and PRS qs , respectively. The second relaxation, ⊥-pseudodeterminism, relaxes the determinism requirement by allowing the output to be a special symbol ⊥ on an inverse-polynomial fraction of inputs. We demonstrate an equivalence between bounded-query logarithmicsize PRS qs , logarithmic-size PRS qs , and PRG qs. Moreover, we establish that PRG qs can be constructed from ⊥-PRGs, which in turn were built from logarithmic-size PRS. Interestingly, these relations remain unknown in the uniform key setting. To further justify these relaxed models, we present black-box separations. Our results suggest that ⊥-pseudodeterministic primitives may be weaker than their deterministic counterparts, and that primitives based on quantum input sampling may be inherently weak er than those using uniform sampling. Together, these results provide numerous new insights into the structure and hierarchy of primitives within MicroCrypt. M.
